newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Agouron sees US approval of AIDS drug.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Agouron sees US approval of AIDS drug.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc is optimistic that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration will approve its Viracept AIDS drug, President and Chief Executive Officer Peter Johnson said on Thursday.
Johnson said he expected the FDA to rule on its application during the first half of this year. He said Viracept "would take on a significant role in combination AIDS therapy" if it was approved.
He said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of Viracept capturing 20 to 25 percent of the market for protease inhibitors, a class of drug for treating AIDS.
He said estimates for the total market for protease inhibitors range from $1 billion to $3 billion a year.

Protease inhibitors work by blocking the AIDS virus from escaping from the patient's DNA when it is about to invade the rest of the body. Currently, the most aggressive AIDS treatment is a three-drug "cocktail" combining a protease inhibitor with two other drugs that attack the virus at an earlier stage in its replication process.
Johnson said the market for protease inhibitors could grow significantly if a new two-drug therapy being tested is shown to be superior to current treatments.

The two-drug therapy would involve two different brands of protease inhibitors. Agouron on Thursday said preliminary data showed Viracept combined with another protease inhibitor "may be a useful therapy."
Citing other studies that showed such a therapy could drive down viral load by as much as 99.9 percent, Johnson said Agouron planned to study the combination further.
Johnson also said he expected an FDA ruling in the first half of 1997 on its application for approval of its powder formulation of Viracept for children. Tests have shown the drug is well tolerated.

"My own overview of the (Viracept trial) data taken together strongly suggests it is one of the most potent of the HIV drugs and has one of the most benign safety profiles, and a very favorable profile of resistance," Johnson said.
Earlier Thursday, Agouron released a variety of data on tests of Viracept in combination with various AIDS drugs.
